lead.headline: Malachi Johnson scores 39 and Idaho State jumps five spots
lead.deck: Idaho State beat South Dakota State 86-71 as a 5.5-point underdog, then covered at Boise State. The rest of the Big Sky went 5-11 in games with a posted line.
body: Idaho State came into the week 10th in the Big Sky power rankings and left fifth. Malachi Johnson had 39 points and 13 rebounds in an 86-71 home win over South Dakota State, where the Bengals were 5.5-point underdogs and won by 15. MaCarhy Morris added 16 points and six assists. Four days later at Boise State the Bengals were 19.5-point underdogs, lost 88-71 and still beat the number.

Montana State stays first in the power rankings and first in our model, 97th nationally at plus-8.2 points per 100 possessions. Its only game this week was a 110-43 win over Northwest Indian, which says nothing. The league's preseason poll, per bigskyconf.com, made the Bobcats the favorite, and the numbers haven't argued.

Portland State had the strangest week in the league. The Vikings were 5-point favorites at home against Cal State Fullerton and lost 92-75. Three days later they won 72-65 at UC Riverside as 2.5-point underdogs, with Yaroslav Nikonov scoring 19 and Koren Johnson 18. The model still has them second in the league, 146th nationally.

Northern Colorado found its scorers. Langston Reynolds, the Big Sky's preseason pick for MVP, had 28 in an 89-66 win over Justice. Jeremiah Hammond went for 34 in a 93-83 win at Detroit Mercy, where the Bears were 5-point favorites and covered. In between they lost 70-60 at home to SE Louisiana as 2.5-point favorites. The model has them 334th, which is a long way from where those two guards are playing.

Overall, the league went 10-11 this week, and 5-11 in the 16 games that had a line. Against the spread it was 6-7 with three pushes. Conference play opens Thursday with five games, and Idaho sits on top of the standings at 4-3.

column.label: Look Ahead
column.title: One more week of road trips, then the league starts
body: **Idaho at Washington State, Friday, 8 p.m.** The only Big Sky game this week with a line, and it isn't kind: the Cougars are 11-point favorites, total 148.5. Idaho won its last two at home, 84-81 over Cal State Bakersfield as a 2-point favorite and 88-47 over Dickinson State. Hudson Ward led the first with 18 and Kase Wynott the second with 21.

**Montana State at South Dakota, Monday, 8 p.m.** The best team in the league by our numbers, on the road against a Summit team that just won 74-73 at Utah Tech. No line posted yet. The Bobcats need a real road win to back up the rating.

**Montana at Arizona State, Monday, 9 p.m.** The Grizzlies fell from third to eighth in the power rankings and the model has them 266th. The Missoulian called the Kansas State loss a blowout. No line posted yet. A good place to make a point.

notes.headline: Northern Arizona lost by one again
notes.body: The Lumberjacks lost 89-88 at Cal Poly as 8-point underdogs. Ryan Abelman scored 33 and Chris Komin had 24 points and 10 assists.

notes.headline: Southern Utah's long week
notes.body: The Thunderbirds lost 104-102 at Arkansas State, 81-66 at FIU and 65-64 at Long Beach State. Jaiden Feroah had 20 points and 11 rebounds in the shootout.

notes.headline: Weber State split
notes.body: The Wildcats beat Tarleton State 89-87 as 2-point favorites, a push, then lost 89-67 at home to Cal State Northridge.

notes.headline: Circle it: Idaho at Northern Colorado
notes.body: Thursday, 8 p.m. ET on ESPN+. The first conference game for both, and the league's top record visits Langston Reynolds and Jeremiah Hammond. No line posted yet.
